title: Star-forming region IC 348 (NIRCam image)
caption: The star-forming region IC 348, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: IC 348 · constellation Perseus · about 1000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Webb, NASA, CSA, K. Luhman, C. Alves De Oliveira, M. Zamani (ESA/Webb)

recognition.text: Ranked #1 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Thick clouds of gas and dust swirl across this scene, dotted with bright stars that each wear six long spikes, a pattern made by the optics of the telescope's mirrors. The densest knot of stars sits near the middle. This is IC 348, a star-forming region about 1000 light-years away, and the picture is one of the largest Webb has released to the public so far.

Hidden among the stars are brown dwarfs, objects smaller than the smallest true stars. Using the sensitivity of its Near-Infrared Camera, Webb hunted down the tiniest brown dwarfs in the region, some only about twice the mass of Jupiter.
No lighter brown dwarfs are known. That they exist at all is a puzzle, because current models of how stars form struggle to explain how such small objects can form in the same way that stars do.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (16.09 x 19.92 arcminutes) and distance (1000 light years), the frame spans roughly 4.7 × 5.8 light-years. Its light set out about 1,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This is a near-infrared image from Webb's NIRCam. The two shortest-wavelength filters are shown in blue, the middle filter in green and the longest in red.
understand.eye: Near-infrared light is invisible to the human eye, so these colors are a translation of wavelengths we cannot see.

explore: In the upper right, a handful of protostars are shooting out long, glowing jets. Where those jets have plowed into the surrounding gas and dust they create bright patches known as Herbig-Haro objects, and Webb gives an unusual view of them.
alt: Swirling clouds of gas and dust scattered with bright six-pointed stars, densest at the center, with long glowing jets in the upper right.
